newsitem.title: USA: SAIC/Bellcore merger expected to close in 1997.
newsitem.headline: SAIC/Bellcore merger expected to close in 1997.

text.p: Science Applications International Corp's (SAIC) proposed purchase of Bell Communications Research Inc, estimated at about $700 million, should close in the latter half of 1997, officials said.

"Our view is that the consummation will happen in the latter half of 1997," said Marty Kaplan, president of Network Services Group, Pacific Bell, and spokesperson for the board of Bellcore, the research and engineering arm of the seven regional Bell telephone companies.
On a conference call, company officials declined comment on reports the deal was valued at about $700 million.

SAIC chief financial officer Bill Roper said the deal requires regulatory approval in nine states where customers are located. Bellcore currently is owned by Ameritech Corp, Bell Atlantic Corp, BellSouth Corp, NYNEX Corp, Pacific Telesis Group, SBC Communications and U S West Inc.
Bellcore, which will remain in independent unit of SAIC, will change its name.
"The Bell name is considered by the owners to be an asset and part of the agreement of the sale is that that asset would not be part of the sale," said Kaplan.

Employee-owned SAIC provides high-technology products and services to government and private industry and has annual revenues exceeding $2.2 billion. SAIC and its subsidiaries have 22,000 employees in more than 475 locations worldwide.
Roper said Bellcore's 5,600 employees will be invited to participate in SAIC's employee stock ownership plan on completion of the deal.

"We've had 27 years of increasing earnings and revenues and the stock price reflects our growth. The compound return on the securities over the years has been in the high teens," Roper said. He said the stock's value was $22.83 a share.
Roper said most of the methods of stock ownership were voluntary and more than half of SAIC's employees now participate in the program.
He said there were no plans for downsizing related to the transaction, noting SAIC currently has in excess of a 1,000 openings, primarily for software people and systems engineers.

"There are opportunities or tasks that Bellcore (employees) can do if not better than SAIC, but there are certain areas where we have some shortages in Bellcore where we'll be able to fill from SAIC," one official said.
While officials declined to comment on the terms of the deal, they said the proceeds would be split evenly among the Bell companies.
About 80 percent of Bellcore's revenues derive from the regional bells.
"I would imagine that the percentage will go down as we grow our non-reginal bell revenues, but let me assure that they will remain our major customers." Kaplan said.
Roper called the deal an additive transaction, with respect to revenues.
